metadata.title: Loud by Default.
metadata.note: Weekly update (changelog framing). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'Vendor Intelligence'. Two tickets: (1) replace print with structured logging — 225 print() calls, zero logging; a silent print hid a broken Langfuse handler (plus phantom traces + fail-open check); 76 prints → logging across 9 files; 83 CLI report-prints kept; levels by what the code does next (WARNING degraded/continuing, ERROR work lost, INFO progress); automated pass got levels wrong (37 err/29 info), fixed by hand; LOG_LEVEL=WARNING drops noise. (2) Validated Settings class — 36 scattered os.getenv with inline defaults → silent wrong config; new collector/settings.py (149 lines); blank = absent; require() reports all missing keys at once; grouped by concern; absorbed and DELETED collector/models.py (committed 72a97a5 last week — intentional, reverses prior work). Verified: 12 modules import cleanly (both import styles), 17 unit tests pass. Bookends render; body B01-B04 are house-style 4K PIL cards (make_cards.py). DOUBLE-CHECK LAW: figures from the creator's change log; dual-path-import ugliness and the stale BEDROCK_MODEL landmine noted in PEDAGOGY, kept off the cards to stay tight.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. This one starts with a real incident. Our observability was broken for who knows how long, and nobody noticed, because the warning was a print statement that scrolled past in a terminal no one was watching. So this week: two fixes that make problems actually show up. Real logging, and config that fails loudly.

props.command: A warning nobody saw broke our observability for weeks — how do I make problems actually show up?
output: a print is invisible to alerts

beats.narration_text: First, the logging. The codebase had two hundred twenty-five print statements and zero logging. And a print is invisible, you can't filter it, alert on it, or ship it to a dashboard. That one blind spot didn't just hide the Langfuse bug, it also hid the phantom traces and the fail-open entity check from earlier. Three bugs, one root cause: nobody could see the warnings.

show.event: the four problem cards snap in

card.title: 225 Prints, Zero Logs.
card.subtitle: a print is invisible

items.quote: no filter, no alert, no dashboard
Langfuse broke — the warning was a print

card.caption: a warning nobody can filter is a warning nobody sees
card.footer: ONE BLIND SPOT, THREE HIDDEN BUGS

beats.narration_text: So I converted seventy-six prints to real logging across nine files. I kept eighty-three, the CLI tools, where the printed report is the actual product, not a diagnostic. And levels were set by what the code does next, not the words in the message: WARNING means degraded but continuing, ERROR means this work was lost, INFO is just progress. An automated pass got this badly wrong, so I fixed every level by hand. Now, log level WARNING drops the noise and keeps the problems.

show.at: set by what the code does next

card.title: Levels by What It Does.
card.subtitle: 76 prints → logging, across 9 files

items.quote: this unit of work was lost
CLI prints — the report IS the product

card.caption: level set by what the code does next, not the words in the message

beats.narration_text: Second, configuration. There were thirty-six scattered get-env calls, each with its own inline default. So a missing or wrong value would surface wherever it happened to get read, usually deep in some tool call, as a confusing error about something unrelated. And a mistyped key? It silently fell back to the default, and the whole system ran on wrong configuration, quietly.

show.event: the four problem cards snap in

card.title: 36 Scattered Getenvs.
card.subtitle: config with no guardrails

items.quote: a confusing error about something else
silently falls back to the default

card.caption: a wrong value surfaced wherever it got read — often far from the real cause

beats.narration_text: The fix is one validated settings file. Every environment value lives in one place now. A blank value counts as missing, not as a valid empty string. And instead of failing halfway through a run, it checks everything up front, require reports every missing key at once, so a misconfigured run stops before it writes a single row. It also absorbed last week's models file, so config lives in one module, not two.

card.title: One Validated Settings.
card.subtitle: fail at startup, not halfway
card.caption: require() reports every missing key up front — so a bad run stops before it writes rows
card.footer: ONE MODULE · GROUPED BY CONCERN · ABSORBED models.py

beats.narration_text: The theme, again: make problems visible. A warning you can't filter is a warning you won't see, and config that fails silently fails at the worst possible time. Log by what the code does, validate config up front, and fail loud.

artifactLines: 225 print() calls, zero logging — a silent print hid a broken Langfuse handler for an unknown time.
76 prints → structured logging across 9 files (CLI report-prints kept); levels by what the code does next.
36 scattered os.getenv → one validated settings.py; blank = absent; require() reports every missing key at once.
Note: this absorbs and deletes models.py from last week — intentional; settings.py supersedes it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Find one print in your code that's really a warning or an error, something you'd want to be alerted on. And find one get-env with an inline default. Then ask: if that value were missing or mistyped, would I find out at startup, or deep in a run, disguised as some unrelated error? Loud and early beats silent and late.
